correctness.rationale: Under j∈{1/2,1,3/2,…}, d=2j+1 and normalized trace-1 Choi construction, the vectorization/partial-transpose flip identity and local time-reversal unitary make C_j^{T2} isospectral to [1/(d j(j+1))](Σ_a J_a⊗J_a)F. Casimir coupling is [L(L+1)−2j(j+1)]/2 on each spin-L subspace, dim=2L+1, with swap parity (−1)^{2j−L}. Thus every claimed eigenvalue and multiplicity follows. The full weighted q-sum Σ_{L=0}^{2j}(2L+1)[L(L+1)−2j(j+1)] vanishes, and the partial sum to L=k−1 equals k²[(k²−1)/2−2j(j+1)] with k=ceil((sqrt(1+8j(j+1))−1)/2); hence the stated trace norm and negativity including exact zero boundary. x=2L+1,y=2j+1 yields Pell x²−2y²=−1; the converse positive solutions satisfy 0≤L≤2j automatically and first nontrivial j are 2,14,84. j=1/2, j=1 boundaries are covered. Inspected all seven assigned Git blobs and reconstructed actual Git tree SHA. Original verify.py checked spin matrices and normalized Choi PT for j=1/2,…,4 and Pell j≤500; independent fresh dense-matrix eigenvalue reconstruction for 13 half-integer/integer spins j≤13/2 agreed. Finite cases corroborate the analytic proof only.
residual_risks: The independent numerical eigenvalue checks are finite and not independent infinite proofs; all-j correctness relies on standard representation-theoretic eigenvalue and swap parity identities.
The theorem concerns the normalized Choi state and one chosen partial transpose, not PPT in every covariant channel or capacities.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: In the 2026 general SU(2)-covariant channel theorem, take the single J=1 Kraus sector with α_1=1/3 (the condition Σ(2J+1)α_J=1). The orthonormal rank-1 spherical tensors are normalized spin generators, so Q_1 = sum_{M=-1}^1 T_{1M} tensor T_{1M}^dagger = [3/((2j+1)j(j+1))] sum_{a=1}^3 J_a tensor J_a. Eqs. (18), (23)–(24) with spin time reversal give C_j^{T_2} unitarily equivalent to (1/3) Q_1 F = [1/((2j+1)j(j+1))](sum_a J_a⊗J_a) F. That is precisely the nontrivial operator identity in the submitted RESULT.md. The standard Casimir eigenvalue (L(L+1)-2j(j+1))/2 and swap parity (-1)^{2j-L} yield every claimed λ_L and multiplicity. The remaining negativity formula is the elementary weighted finite sum; zero eigenvalues reduce by x=2L+1,y=2j+1 to x²−2y²=−1. Thus all three asserted outcomes are mathematical consequences of the earlier general published operator identity with routine spin algebra, not merely similar terminology or a partial overlap.

originality.rationale: Strong prior mathematical implication discovered from a primary paper published 2026-07-05, before the 2026-10-12 research record. Rudnicki et al. give a complete general Choi projector and rank-J tensor-operator/partial-transpose identity for all SU(2)-covariant channels; specialization to α_1=1/3 reproduces exactly the operator diagonalized in this submission. Applying the textbook Casimir+flip eigenvalues gives the claimed all-spin spectrum, and the claimed negativity and negative Pell classification are elementary arithmetic consequences. Schliemann 2005 also establishes a much broader existing formalism for all eigenvalues of the partial transpose of SU(2)-invariant spin states. Neither preprint nor paper needs to print the present formula to imply it. Original self-review omitted decisive July 2026 coverage. Resultary returned no exact table; negative search does not overturn the source-level mathematical implication.
residual_risks: The explicit arithmetic Pell subsequence may not be printed in the covering paper, but it is exactly the root condition of its implied Casimir/flip spectrum; this is mathematical implication rather than verbatim duplication.

Original RESULT.md proof and its weighted-sum/Pell steps
value.rationale: The normalized spin-channel Choi negativity and Pell singularity locus are natural quantities and useful for exposition, but the exact spectrum is an immediate rank-one-tensor (J=1) special case of the already published 2026 SU(2)-covariant Choi partial-transpose identity with the standard Casimir eigenvalues. The negativity formula is evaluation of a basic polynomial finite sum and the Pell set merely rewrites the zero of that existing sector eigenvalue. No independent nonstandard structural lemma, new undetermined invariant, unknown arithmetic cutoff, counterexample or calculation not mechanically implied by the stronger antecedent survives. The Pell observation can be instructive but is not a separately motivated valuable theorem under the stated bar.
residual_risks: Some readers may find the explicit negativity and Pell phrasing useful pedagogically even though these are direct corollaries, not independent scientific contribution.
This value judgment concerns the claimed new research finding, not the utility of teaching examples.

limitations: No proof of channel capacities, distillable entanglement or general SU(2) channel negativity.
Originality rejected by a stronger earlier published mathematical implication, not merely by absence of explicit source wording or a failed literature search.
